name: issue_827_sleep_window_interior_keeps_sleep_mode
description: Issue #827 GAP-5 / #1066 companion to issue_827_sleep_window_floor_mismatch. In the sleep window (sleep_heat 60F, sleep_cool 72F) a warm-day reading of 64F is 4F below the DAYTIME comfort floor (68F) but strictly between sleep floor + m (62F) and sleep ceiling - m (70F). Nearest-edge arming keeps the sleep-window mode (cool at the sleep ceiling) and never commands heat; a selector using the daytime floor would see a breach and heat at 68F.
source: Issue #827 GAP-5 audit; split out during the Issue #1066 review so the interior case can be asserted with whole-run hvac_mode_never_commanded.
notes: Occupant impact: overnight at 64F with a 60F sleep setback the occupant is fine; the furnace must not start at the daytime 68F target.

(a) Scenario effectiveness: with the daytime floor in the selector, 64F < 68F is a floor breach, heat is armed immediately, and hvac_mode_never_commanded(heat) and comfort_family=cooling both fail. With nearest-edge arming deleted (origin/main) a warm day is natively cooling and 64F would also be held, so this scenario guards the floor INPUT (band.floor) and the interior-holds-mode rule, not the old-vs-new difference.
(b) Docs<->production alignment: docs/08 section 6f ('strictly between floor + m and ceiling - m: the thermostat's actual current mode').
(c) Occupant outcome if this test fails to catch a regression: the furnace heats a sleeping household to 68F against their chosen 60F overnight setback.

events.note: Sleep window, indoor 70F: cooling zone (>= 72 - 2), cool armed at the sleep ceiling 72.
Warm-day classification (classifier hvac_mode=off); sleep band [60, 72] armed.
64F: below the daytime floor (68) but strictly between 62 and 70 of the sleep band. Mode is kept.
Re-evaluation at 64F: still cooling at the sleep ceiling, no heat.
Another reading at 64F: still no heat.
Second re-evaluation at 64F: still no heat.

assertions.reason: Baseline: sleep band armed, not the daytime band.
Heat is never commanded anywhere in the run: 64F is above the sleep floor + margin, so neither a 60F nor a 68F heat setpoint is sent.
Final engine state: the sleep-window cooling family is kept in the interior; a daytime-floor selector would have switched to heating at the 64F reading.
The last climate command is the cool setpoint at the sleep ceiling (72F).

verdict.summary: A 64F overnight reading (below the daytime floor, inside the sleep band's interior) keeps the sleep-window mode and never starts heat.
verdict.observed_behavior: Cool at 72F is armed at 70F and re-affirmed at 64F with no heat command.
verdict.expected_behavior: The selector uses the resolved sleep band and holds the current mode strictly between the arming margins.
